rationales: Goldstein’s canal-ray experiments revealed positive particles and are credited with proton discovery in this curriculum.
J. J. Thomson discovered the electron, not the proton.
Bohr proposed a model of the atom and did not discover the proton.
Rutherford later identified the hydrogen nucleus as the proton, but this question’s expected answer is Goldstein.
Cesium is the most reactive of the listed alkali metals.
Rubidium is reactive but less reactive than cesium.
Potassium is reactive but less reactive than rubidium and cesium.
Sodium is less reactive than the other listed alkali metals.
One mole of H₂SO₄ has a mass of 98 g, conventionally expressed as 98 g/mol.
98 amu is the molecular mass, not the molar mass.
9.8 g is one tenth of the mass of a mole of H₂SO₄.
9.8 amu is far below the molecular mass of H₂SO₄.
This is the value in milligrams, not grams, and is too small by a factor of 1000.
One atomic mass unit is approximately 1.66×10⁻²⁴ g.
This is the value in kilograms, not the standard gram equivalent.
This is ten times larger than the value of one atomic mass unit in grams.
The s-block contains the alkali and alkaline-earth elements, not the lanthanides and actinides.
The p-block contains elements in groups 13–18, not these series.
The d-block contains the transition elements, while lanthanides and actinides are f-block elements.
Lanthanides and actinides are the f-block series.
Pure ethanol boils at about 78 °C, not 70 °C.
100 °C is the boiling point of water at standard pressure.
0 °C is near water’s freezing point, not alcohol’s boiling point.
Ethanol’s boiling point is approximately 78 °C.
Donation of an electron alone describes electron transfer, not covalent bonding.
Acceptance of electrons alone describes electron transfer, not covalent bonding.
A covalent bond forms when atoms share electron pairs.
Repulsion of electrons does not form a covalent bond.
Starch solution contains starch and is not concentrated sodium chloride solution.
Chloride solution is not the usual name for concentrated sodium chloride solution.
A concentrated sodium chloride solution is called brine.
Carbonated solution contains dissolved carbon dioxide, not concentrated sodium chloride.
Calcium is denser than water and does not float on it.
Sodium is less dense than water and floats on it.
Magnesium is denser than water and does not float on it.
Potassium is also less dense than water and floats on it, so both sodium and potassium fit and the question is ambiguous.
The molecular mass of H₂O is 18 amu.
18 g is the mass of one mole of water, not the molecular mass unit requested.
18 mg is not the molecular mass of water.
18 kg is not the molecular mass of water.
Eight grams of CO₂ is about 0.18 mol, not 0.15 mol.
8 ÷ 44 ≈ 0.18 mol of CO₂.
0.21 mol would correspond to more than 8 g of CO₂.
0.24 mol would correspond to more than 8 g of CO₂.
This configuration has 5 electrons, not fluorine’s 9.
This configuration has 8 electrons, not fluorine’s 9.
This configuration has 7 electrons, not fluorine’s 9.
Fluorine has 9 electrons, with configuration 1s² 2s² 2p⁵.
Mendeleev’s principle was based on atomic mass, not the basis of the modern long-form table.
The long-form periodic table is arranged by increasing atomic number.
Atomic mass is not the organizing basis of the modern long-form table.
Mass number is not the organizing basis of the periodic table.
Metallic bonding involves attraction between metal ions and delocalized electrons, not simple transfer between atoms.
Electron transfer between atoms produces oppositely charged ions that form an ionic bond.
Covalent bonding involves sharing electrons rather than transferring them.
A coordinate covalent bond forms when one atom donates a shared electron pair.
C₂H₂ contains a carbon–carbon triple covalent bond.
HCl has a single covalent bond.
CH₄ contains four single covalent bonds.
NaCl forms an ionic bond, not a triple covalent bond.
